body.x: AETECH (CEO Taehyung Park) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas, USA, at the K-Startup Pavilion.

Founded in 2020, AETECH is a startup dedicated to building smart cities where robots sort waste. The company developed and launched Atron, an AI-based recycling robot, as part of its vision to revolutionize the resource recycling sector through cutting-edge technology.

Building on this success, AETECH plans to introduce a broader waste management solution by launching Airo-mrf (AI Robot Material Recovery Facility) in 2025. This automated sorting facility, centered around robotic operations, aims to enhance resource recovery and efficiency.
At CES 2025, AETECH will present Atron and Airo-mrf to global audiences, laying the groundwork for international expansion in the resource recycling sector.

Atron is an AI-driven robot designed to sort and recover waste autonomously. It has been trained on over 2.8 million waste data samples collected from actual sorting facilities and continues to improve its learning. The current model can sort up to 43 types of recyclable waste—such as PET, PP, and PE—based on material and color, achieving a sorting accuracy of 99.3% and handling up to 96 items per minute. These capabilities have allowed waste facilities using Atron to reduce sorting costs by up to 279% and cut processing time by 126%, according to AETECH.

body.cap: AETECH's waste-sorting smart factory, 'Airo-mrf' | Photo provided by AETECH

body.x: Airo-mrf represents AETECH's vision for waste-sorting smart factories. Designed to manage the entire process—from waste loading and sorting to producing recycled materials—the facility employs more than 30 Atron robots. These robots work harmoniously with circular conveyor belts to maximize resource recovery efficiency.

While traditional facilities relying on manual sorting achieve resource recovery rates of 30-40%, Airo-mrf can achieve rates of 70-80%. Additionally, the system reduces annual incineration costs by over KRW 60 million and lowers yearly carbon emissions by approximately 9,215 tons.

An AETECH representative explained, “Atron and Airo-mrf are our two flagship business models, providing efficient, human-centered waste management solutions. They aim to drive innovation in the resource recycling industry and contribute significantly to global sustainability. Moreover, our automated systems create safer and more pleasant working conditions in sorting facilities.”

The representative added, “Through CES 2025, we aim to enhance our brand recognition and value as a technology leader while gaining insights into industry trends. This global stage will also provide invaluable networking opportunities with potential investors and buyers, enabling us to establish a strong foundation for international market entry.”
